source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
A household survey of 250 red-corn (ដំណាំពោតក្រហម) farming households across Kampong Cham, Kandal, Battambang, and Pailin found farmers using at least 53 distinct named corn seed varieties (mostly hybrid brand/code names, many from Vietnamese and Thai seed companies), with no single variety dominating the market.

The most commonly used varieties, with the number of households using them and their share of the sample, were: VN (26 households, 10.4%), CP (23, 9.2%), 339 (20, 8.0%), 999 (20, 8.0%), 99999 (13, 5.2%), VN10 (13, 5.2%), 22 (12, 4.8%), T63 (12, 4.8%), 222 (11, 4.4%), 95 (10, 4.0%), 30B80 (8, 3.2%), Phkar Mles (7, 2.8%), 54 (6, 2.4%), 6326 (6, 2.4%), 7328 (4, 1.6%), 9889 (4, 1.6%), Kajas Keu (4, 1.6%), 722 (3, 1.2%), 800 (3, 1.2%), 88 (3, 1.2%), 888 (3, 1.2%), and M23 (3, 1.2%). A long tail of roughly 30 additional varieties (4859, 939, 96, Thai, Chomros, 101, 1295, 2663, 333, 4858, 555, 598&509, 61801, 63826, 66&55, 7326, 754, 80, 880, 8888, 8889, 9999, CP&VN10, CP888, DK, GP222, HP99, NTR, Pasific, PP88, SSS) were each used by only 1-2 households (0.4-0.8% of the sample).

As for where farmers get their seed, 46% (114 households) buy from village-level dealers, 25% (62) buy seed imported from Vietnam, 24% (60) buy seed imported from Thailand, and 6% (14) get seed from farming/agribusiness companies.
